environment.description: Application deployed behind Cloudflare with the following zone-level configuration: (1) Rate Limiting Rule on path /account/* with threshold of 3 requests per 10-second window per IP, action=block returning 429 for 60 seconds. (2) Cloudflare Bot Management enabled with bot score threshold 30 (requests scoring below 30 are challenged with managed challenge). (3) Cloudflare 'Super Bot Fight Mode' set to 'Definitely Automated' = Block, 'Likely Automated' = Managed Challenge. The rate limit specifically targets the /account/ path prefix which covers change-password and update-email. CSRF exploitation requires the victim's browser to make the cross-origin request, but the attacker cannot control timing — if the victim has made any legitimate account requests in the prior 10 seconds, subsequent CSRF-triggered requests will be rate-limited. More critically, automated CSRF exploitation tools and headless browsers used for testing/chaining will be blocked by bot management before reaching the application. The combination means: single-shot CSRF from a real browser might succeed once, but any repeated exploitation (password change + email change chain, or retry after failure) triggers the 429 block, and automated exploitation frameworks are blocked entirely by bot scoring.

config.cookie_samesite: Lax (enforced by browser due to HTTPS + Secure flag via Cloudflare)
